label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
The Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms ended on Saturday, and I'm still smiling about it. It ran from 5 to 7 November in Seminar Hall 2 at the Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. I was one of the three organisers, and I'm posting this on behalf of the team (Ketaki Joglekar, Faizan Mirza and me) to say thank you.

A few numbers. We received 112 applications and selected 41 participants, MSc and early PhD students from 9 states, on the basis of a statement and one reference. An institute student initiative grant of Rs 2.4 lakh covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students.

Thank you to Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, our faculty mentor, for backing a student-run school and guiding us throughout. Thank you to our speakers: Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) on Mordell-Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) on modular forms, and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined online from Kraków to teach computations in Sage.

Thank you to Mr. Prakash Salunke from the office, who sorted out our hostel rooms at 11 pm when the booking got messed up. And thank you to the six PhD students who did TA work and ran the problem sessions. Those sessions worked really well, and we'll keep that format.

Two moments I'll remember. On day 2 the power went out for nearly two hours in the afternoon and the laptops died. We moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards, and it turned out to be the best session of the three days. And an MSc student from Silchar found an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma'am's notes. She corrected it live and thanked him.

Moments like these are why I think small schools matter more than big conferences for MSc students. They get to actually ask questions. Thank you to all 41 participants for coming with exactly that energy.

Slides and problem sheets will go up on the department website in about two weeks. We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, depending on whether the grant comes through. If it does, we'd love to see you there.

Thank you, everyone, for three days of good mathematics.
